## Claims
- [source-backed] The recorded two families are \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) and \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), where \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\), with \(q=n-r\). [source-6, lines 18-42]
- [proved] The requested standalone integral transpose-reduction lemma is established: it identifies the theorem-displayed first family at \((r,q;i,j)\) with the Remark 4.7 second family at \((q,r;j,i)\), descends to Grassmannian quotients, and preserves minimality.

## Strategy
Let
\[
A_{r,q}:=\Lambda/I_{r,q},\qquad
I_{r,q}:=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda .
\]
The integral Schur involution \(\omega:\Lambda\to\Lambda\), defined by
\(\omega(h_d)=e_d\), satisfies \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\).
Since
\[
\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\iff \lambda'\nsubseteq r^q,
\]
one has \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\). Hence \(\omega\) descends to an
integral graded ring isomorphism
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r},
\qquad \bar s_\lambda\longmapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}.
\]

Assume \(0\le i\le q\), \(0\le j\le r\), and set
\[
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j).
\]
Define
\[
\mathcal B_{r,q;i,j}
=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\},
\]
\[
\mathcal T_{r,q;i,j}
=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu
 \subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{\,j-b})\}.
\]
All partitions involved lie in \(q^r\): \(a\le q-i,r-j\) and
\(b\le i,j\).

Put
\[
(r',q';i',j')=(q,r;j,i).
\]
Then
\[
a'=\min(q'-i',r'-j')=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad
b'=\min(i',j')=b.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(i^j,b^a)'=((j+a)^b,j^{\,i-b}),
\]
so partition containment and transposition give
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}\bigl(\mathcal B_{r,q;i,j}\bigr)
=
\mathcal T_{q,r;j,i}.
\]
Thus the theorem-displayed family \(\mathcal B\) is carried exactly to
the Remark 4.7 family \(\mathcal T\) with the stated transformed
parameters. Conversely,
\[
((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})'=(j^i,b^a),
\]
so \(\bar\omega_{r,q}(\mathcal T_{r,q;i,j})
=\mathcal B_{q,r;j,i}\).

For bigrassmannian parameters
\[
v=v_{r,s,t,n},\qquad q=n-r,
\]
the same transformation is
\[
(r',s',t',n')=(q,n-s,q-s+t,n).
\]
Indeed,
\[
i'=s'-t'+1=r-t+1=j,\qquad
j'=r'-t'+1=s-t+1=i.
\]
The usual inequalities \(1\le t\le r,s\) and \(t>r+s-n\) imply
\(1\le t'\le r',s'\), so the transformed data are admissible.

Finally, if \(J_{r,q;i,j}\) denotes the corresponding interval ideal,
then \(\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}\). A ring isomorphism
takes a generating subfamily to a generating subfamily, and its inverse
takes proper subfamilies to proper subfamilies. Therefore a family is
minimal as an ideal generating family if and only if its transpose image
is minimal. In particular, minimality of the theorem family for the
dual parameters implies minimality of the Remark 4.7 family for the
original parameters.

## Gaps
The lemma is a reduction only; it does not independently prove the
minimality theorem used as its input.

## Next
